entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“King Romus is interested in increa..."
entries.dialogueText: “King Romus is interested in increasing energy independence and diversifying his energy assets. Our sources indicate that he wants to acquire control of more natural gas resources.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I'm cynical about monarchies. Thei..."
entries.dialogueText: “I'm cynical about monarchies. Their time in Merkopa seems to be running out, and their stability is in question.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We are still facing the potential..."
entries.dialogueText: “We are still facing the potential of a recession. New avenues for trade could help keep our books balanced.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Isn't this unusual? Aren't you and..."
entries.dialogueText: “Isn't this unusual? Aren't you and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in charge of arranging negotiations?”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“The Toras and Livingston families..."
entries.dialogueText: “The Toras and Livingston families should be considered allies for the time being. However, from a practical standpoint, they are too far from each other to provide military support.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Classic Wild Gus. Even before we s..."
entries.dialogueText: “Classic Wild Gus. Even before we started campaigning, he was in the game non-stop. Gus, connecting people.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Self-reliant monarchies like Rumbu..."
entries.dialogueText: “Self-reliant monarchies like Rumburg are much more likely to last. But for the time being, many of the international monarchs have close ties and trade with each other to avoid revolution and change.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Both countries are also part of th..."
entries.dialogueText: “Both countries are also part of the worldwide network of monarchies known as GRACE. The framework is mostly financially and politically motivated due to the pressures of Malenyevism and democracy.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Rizia is a developed nation with a..."
entries.dialogueText: “Rizia is a developed nation with a resilient economy thanks to its gold wealth. They can aid Sordland's economic health and the fiscal pain points Minister Holl keeps highlighting.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Usually, yes, but in special scena..."
entries.dialogueText: “Usually, yes, but in special scenarios such as this, real and close connections between people can improve the likelihood of a positive outcome. Since Mr. Manger has the strongest relations with the envoy, we have assigned staff to him to help with the talks.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“The international web of monarchie..."
entries.dialogueText: “The international web of monarchies and sympathizers across all the continents of Merkopa, Rika, Xina, Contana have united under The Guild of Royal Allies for Commercial Exchange.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“We must take into account Rizia’s..."
entries.dialogueText: “We must take into account Rizia’s blood ties and de facto alliance with Rumburg. The King married into the Livingston family. Geographically, Rizia and Rumburg are too far to help each other; their only actual link is through sea lanes passing by Sordland.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“I'm sure if Gus is involved, the d..."
entries.dialogueText: “I'm sure if Gus is involved, the deal will be financially viable. His connections in the business world are vast.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“As Minister Holl rightfully descri..."
entries.dialogueText: “As Minister Holl rightfully described, we must do everything in our power not to fall into debt with an unhealthy economy.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“But as long as we are getting a go..."
entries.dialogueText: “But as long as we are getting a good offer, it doesn’t matter who officially leads the negotiation. I’m sure Mr. Wisci doesn’t mind.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“We should be more concerned with-”"
entries.dialogueText: “We should be more concerned with-”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Regardless, ideological or politic..."
entries.dialogueText: “Regardless, ideological or political motivations are less of a concern. We need to assess what Sordland stands to benefit from a potential agreement.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“If Rizia wants to buy more than 20..."
entries.dialogueText: “If Rizia wants to buy more than 20 percent of shares allowed by the protectionism laws, then the government can step in to make changes to the EPA.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Precisely, but we don’t know if th..."
entries.dialogueText: “Precisely, but we don’t know if this will be the case. There is a scenario in which they might invest within the EPA limitations; we just have to hear more before weighing the options.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“The military should also be funded..."
entries.dialogueText: “The military should also be funded appropriately if additional resources are to be acquired.”

entries.dialogueText: “We have no close contacts with the Toras royals anymore. It leaves us little option but to use the back channel of Mr. Manger and President Alphonso.”

entries.speaker: Player

entries.dialogueText: “*Former* President Alphonso.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“That sounds good to me.”"
entries.dialogueText: “That sounds good to me.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Ah, yes, Mr. President. Excuse me...."
entries.dialogueText: “Ah, yes, Mr. President. Excuse me. Former President Alphonso.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Very well.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Very well.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“From what we have gathered, there..."
entries.dialogueText: “From what we have gathered, there is no clear offer yet. The interest clearly seems to be more control over the gas produced and sold in Sordland. I suspect this must be related to the recent tensions on the coast of Pales.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“That must be related to Gasom oper..."
entries.dialogueText: “That must be related to Gasom operations. Gus has ties with the people around that corporation. Even though there is another CEO, Ewald Alphonso is still chairman.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“I suspect that the corporation isn..."
entries.dialogueText: “I suspect that the corporation isn’t doing too well, and they are seeking investments. Any investment into Gasom will enrich the owners but might also lead to more jobs and growth.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Why deal with a monarchy? They've..."
entries.dialogueText: “Why deal with a monarchy? They've sucked enough blood from the people of Merkopa.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Strong words, Anton. I like it!”"
entries.dialogueText: “Strong words, Anton. I like it!”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“From a humanistic standpoint, with..."
entries.dialogueText: “From a humanistic standpoint, without the general population participating in governance, equality problems arise. Yet these countries are here to stay.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Mr. Manger is working out the deta..."
entries.dialogueText: “Mr. Manger is working out the details to get more concrete headline terms soon. Of particular interest are the gas fields in the Narbel area of the Nargis region.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We should protect our energy indep..."
entries.dialogueText: “We should protect our energy independence, but we don’t know the offer's specifics yet.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Affluent Sords don’t stray far fro..."
entries.dialogueText: “Affluent Sords don’t stray far from each other.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The shareholder links raise questi..."
entries.dialogueText: “The shareholder links raise questions regarding Alphonso and Manger's motivations.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I agree, but Gasom is a private co..."
entries.dialogueText: “I agree, but Gasom is a private corporation. Even though it mostly supplies the government, we have little control over it.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Why would they? Similar circles, s..."
entries.dialogueText: “Why would they? Similar circles, similar educational background, companies. Half of the oligarchs are from LBS or Harcard.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Gasom is a private corporation, a..."
entries.dialogueText: “Gasom is a private corporation, a fact that limits our control over any foreign investment. Tarquin Soll's Energy Protection Act of 1932 specifically limits the purchases of Sordish energy company shares by foreign nations to ten percent.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“As a sovereign nation, we must pro..."
entries.dialogueText: “As a sovereign nation, we must protect our resources. Our energy independence is part of our national security concern here; Gasom handles most of our gas production.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“As long as we can improve our econ..."
entries.dialogueText: “As long as we can improve our economy and resource extraction, we shouldn’t care much.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I think we must act pragmatically..."
entries.dialogueText: “I think we must act pragmatically in this case. I stand with Mr. Galade, as long as the country stands to benefit economically and there are no human rights concerns.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“I have information that the CEO th..."
entries.dialogueText: “I have information that the CEO that replaced Alphonso is a loyalist. Alphonso still is the chairman of Gasom and the de facto key figure. Additionally, National Business Council Chairman Mikail Aven and Minister Gus Manger have shares in the company and preside over the board.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I look favorably towards a potenti..."
entries.dialogueText: “I look favorably towards a potential investment from Rizia into Sordland.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We will have to wait and hear more..."
entries.dialogueText: “We will have to wait and hear more from Mr. Manger to decide.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“There is strong potential for furt..."
entries.dialogueText: “There is strong potential for further cooperation, and Rizia previously aided Sordland when it needed foreign help the most.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“If there's one thing Gus is good a..."
entries.dialogueText: “If there's one thing Gus is good at, it’s making deals.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Thank you. Our support staff and I..."
entries.dialogueText: “Thank you. Our support staff and I will be working towards the next steps soon after receiving more context from Mr. Manger.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“I will assist in analyzing the pol..."
entries.dialogueText: “I will assist in analyzing the political implications, Mr. Wisci.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Our ambassador in Porte Drazon is..."
entries.dialogueText: “Our ambassador in Porte Drazon is in communication with Laurento Esquibel, the Rizian Councilor of Foreign Affairs, already.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""The nation south of Lespia is a ce..."
entries.dialogueText: "The nation south of Lespia is a centralized constitutional monarchy led by King Romus Toras. The grandson of Queen Lyza Toras, 'the Great', and son of King Valero Toras, 'the Frail'."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“The Alphonso government signed vit..."
entries.dialogueText: “The Alphonso government signed vital trade agreements with King Romus Toras, benefitting both nations at a time of need. Attempts at further cooperation stalled out due to the King's blood ties to Rumburg.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Petr pulled out the ornamental coin..."
entries.dialogueText: Petr pulled out the ornamental coin and put it on the table. It was so polished that it caught reflections of light in the room. Lucian was clearly frustrated.

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“The kingdom is a developed nation..."
entries.dialogueText: “The kingdom is a developed nation that wielded considerable influence in Southern Merkopa before the reign of Valero. The country has lost some territory due to internal strife.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“There is some tension with both. I..."
entries.dialogueText: “There is some tension with both. It appears that since Lespia's acceptance into ATO in 1950, most of South Merkopa has been heading towards a boiling point."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“In the 1930s, King Romus married P..."
entries.dialogueText: “In the 1930s, King Romus married Princess Lena Livingston, the youngest daughter of King Alfred Livingston the Second, sister of Queen Beatrice Livingston.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“What exactly are these blood ties..."
entries.dialogueText: “What exactly are these blood ties between Rizia and Rumburg?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I’m curious how our neighbors Lesp..."
entries.dialogueText: “I’m curious how our neighbors Lespia and Wehlen get along with Rizia.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Actually, a friend of Gus called R..."
entries.dialogueText: “Actually, a friend of Gus called Rusty gifted me this beautiful piece of full Rizian gold coin. They say it helps you find love. Look.”

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I took the coin in my hands and loo..."
entries.dialogueText: I took the coin in my hands and looked at the details.
entries.menuText: Examine the coin.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Not bad. You can't go wrong with g..."
entries.dialogueText: “Not bad. You can't go wrong with gold.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Petr interjected and reached in his..."
entries.dialogueText: Petr interjected and reached in his pocket.

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“It was a political marriage that b..."
entries.dialogueText: “It was a political marriage that benefitted Rizia, helping save it from downfall. The two nations are close, to say the least.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“All these kings and queens disagre..."
entries.dialogueText: “All these kings and queens disagree more than agree, but they're forced to tolerate each other's differences. Imagine if Koronti and the SBC cast the world's remaining monarchs in a soap opera.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I would watch the hell out of that..."
entries.dialogueText: “I would watch the hell out of that.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Lets stay on point.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Lets stay on point.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“This new engagement regarding the..."
entries.dialogueText: “This new engagement regarding the Rizian investment interest is coordinated through our Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development, Gus Manger, and former President Alphonso.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Many are not official allies, but..."
entries.dialogueText: “Many are not official allies, but have economic pacts to secure global independence.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The Kingdom was meant to collapse...."
entries.dialogueText: “The Kingdom was meant to collapse. Nothing could save it, regardless of the effort.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Your father was truly a great man,..."
entries.dialogueText: “Your father was truly a great man, may he rest in peace.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“In the Tarquin Soll period, we nev..."
entries.dialogueText: “In the Tarquin Soll period, we never saw such dependency on foreign nations.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Looking a few years back, they pla..."
entries.dialogueText: “Looking a few years back, they played a significant role in helping Sordland avoid depression. There is merit to this fact.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Former President Alphonso signed t..."
entries.dialogueText: “Former President Alphonso signed trade agreements with King Romus Toras of Rizia. The previous government revived the older relationship that existed during the days of the Sordish monarchy."

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Yes, with the exceptionally succes..."
entries.dialogueText: “Yes, with the exceptionally successful SSC bills, the Soll government raised funds for its autarky plans from the Sordish population alone.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“The Colonel knew the real intentio..."
entries.dialogueText: “The Colonel knew the real intentions of foreign powers. Our strength comes from within. Our greatest resource is our people.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“He deserved a more honorable end.”"
entries.dialogueText: “He deserved a more honorable end.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Independence is important, but as..."
entries.dialogueText: “Independence is important, but as the world is changing and our continental blocs are trading more with one another, we must adapt. There is a place for trade and co-development with nations like Rizia.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Thank you, Anton. I hope our natio..."
entries.dialogueText: “Thank you, Anton. I hope our nation never faces the tragedies of those dark days again. He was the best father one could have wanted.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The room went silent for a moment."
entries.dialogueText: The room went silent for a moment.

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Let's continue our discussion abou..."
entries.dialogueText: “Let's continue our discussion about Rizia.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“King Egmund was far too isolated a..."
entries.dialogueText: “King Egmund was far too isolated and detached. Figures like Heron Walt and Artor S. Wisci spent a great deal of effort attempting to bring him to his senses.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Times change, and any good leader..."
entries.dialogueText: “Times change, and any good leader must make an effort to adapt. The Kingdom indeed had structural flaws that led to the Republic my father founded.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "Our Republic stands on firmer footi..."
entries.dialogueText: Our Republic stands on firmer footing despite these recent troubles than those days.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Edith Agnoc's handling with the Ce..."
entries.dialogueText: "Edith Agnoc's handling with the Central Bank measures to prevent the depression also deserves credit."

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“The relationship between Rizia and..."
entries.dialogueText: “The relationship between Rizia and Wehlen is more complex than that. They were closely aligned under Valero's rule until Rumburg entered the play.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“Not to mention Wehlen's struggles..."
entries.dialogueText: “Not to mention Wehlen's struggles with the BFF, an organization that we've long suspected to be armed by King Romus' in-laws in Rumburg.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We have enough issues to figure ou..."
entries.dialogueText: “We have enough issues to figure out; we can’t worry about the problems of others.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Merkopan geopolitics are a complex..."
entries.dialogueText: “Merkopan geopolitics are a complexity of another caliber.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“My job is to make sense of it. It..."
entries.dialogueText: “My job is to make sense of it. It is a privilege I enjoy, regardless of my age.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“I'll bring the popcorn!”"
entries.dialogueText: “I'll bring the popcorn!”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Sure, sure!”"
entries.dialogueText: “Sure, sure!”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "At the center was the emblem of Riz..."
entries.dialogueText: At the center was the emblem of Rizia, a fierce bull standing on two feet with its horns pointed upwards. In the background was a shield intricately ornamented with leaves and a crown.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "At the bottom, the letters RRG were..."
entries.dialogueText: At the bottom, the letters RRG were engraved.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“What is RRG?”"
entries.dialogueText: “What is RRG?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Nice piece, Petr.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Nice piece, Petr.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Thanks. Maybe I'll turn it into a..."
entries.dialogueText: “Thanks. Maybe I'll turn it into a golden tooth when I get old.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“It's Rizian Royal Gold. The compan..."
entries.dialogueText: “It's Rizian Royal Gold. The company that mines and processes the high-quality ore used to mint the country's gold.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Sure can't.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Sure can't.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Some Rizians who settled for the d..."
entries.dialogueText: “Some Rizians who settled for the deal in the final years of Kingdom still live in the Old Town of Holsord to this day.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“It's good to be informed in the di..."
entries.dialogueText: “It's good to be informed in the diplomacy field. There is always so much movement.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I think this summarizes all we kno..."
entries.dialogueText: “I think this summarizes all we know and what we stand to gain, Mr. President. What are your thoughts?”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I’m curious how it will develop. I..."
entries.dialogueText: “I’m curious how it will develop. It’s mostly out of the hands of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for now.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Deivid hesitated for a brief moment..."
entries.dialogueText: Deivid hesitated for a brief moment.

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“The main negotiator was my father,..."
entries.dialogueText: “The main negotiator was my father, former president Artor S. Wisci, who, with the Republican faction of the King’s parliament, fought to achieve a rare consensus in the heavily fractured council at the time.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Mot He Vest Peasa.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Mot He Vest Peasa.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“It wouldn't be bad to focus on the..."
entries.dialogueText: “It wouldn't be bad to focus on the important job of keeping our farmers and rural population happy.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Let's move on.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Let's move on.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“As you wish, and thank you.”"
entries.dialogueText: “As you wish, and thank you.”

entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Ewald Alphonso adjusted this law i..."
entries.dialogueText: “Ewald Alphonso adjusted this law in 1948 and increased it to up to 20 percent. Anything above that requires us to change the Energy Protection Act. Ewald holds most of Gasom's cards in his hands still.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Remember campaigning for him back..."
entries.dialogueText: “Remember campaigning for him back in the day? He wouldn't have gotten the USP leadership without us.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Things didn't end amicably between..."
entries.dialogueText: “Things didn't end amicably between us. I mean, we aggressively destroyed his campaign team one by one.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“He was right to open up the countr..."
entries.dialogueText: “He was right to open up the country, regardless of what happened in '51. Sordland is in a good position to benefit from world trade.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I see a strong case for Tarquin So..."
entries.dialogueText: “I see a strong case for Tarquin Soll's regulation. Energy security is important for our nation.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Gasom is private, but it still sel..."
entries.dialogueText: “Gasom is private, but it still sells most of the gas it produces to Sordland, right?”

entries.title: Player: "“The way we publicly embarrassed hi..."
entries.dialogueText: “The way we publicly embarrassed him on national television won't help further dialogue.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Good thing, we handled the transfe..."
entries.dialogueText: “Good thing, we handled the transfer of power within the party diplomatically. I'm sure he will be more open to talk.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“His decision not to increase the a..."
entries.dialogueText: “His decision not to increase the armed forces budget for the term was unprecedented. President Soll would always fund our troops a little more.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“We had to break the status quo to..."
entries.dialogueText: “We had to break the status quo to get into government ourselves. I always thought Alphonso was too optimistic about his grand plans.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“We helped him get to power, but al..."
entries.dialogueText: “We helped him get to power, but also led him to his fall. Such a peaceful transition with the '53 elections, however, showed the strength of our democracy.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“I've got to say his team was great..."
entries.dialogueText: “I've got to say his team was great to work with. Toppling Tarquin Soll was a historic moment in the USP.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“Fueling the Rumburg war machine is..."
entries.dialogueText: “Fueling the Rumburg war machine is indisputably wrong.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Up to 70 percent goes to Sordland...."
entries.dialogueText: “Up to 70 percent goes to Sordland. This used to be higher, but international demand has seen Gasom diversify its deliveries outward.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Rumburg and Lespia are increasing..."
entries.dialogueText: “Rumburg and Lespia are increasing their demand each year. They have hungry industries waiting to be fulfilled.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“I think so, yes. Lucian knows more..."
entries.dialogueText: “I think so, yes. Lucian knows more than me.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“This is why I like to stay out of..."
entries.dialogueText: “This is why I like to stay out of politics.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“We reached a successful result and..."
entries.dialogueText: “We reached a successful result and won over the country. The rest is history; it happened. I’m focused on the history we are writing now.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I played little to no part in the..."
entries.dialogueText: “I played little to no part in the last period except for campaigning and helping Anton get the votes.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“It wasn’t my preferred method, Ant..."
entries.dialogueText: “It wasn’t my preferred method, Anton, but it worked. I have to say all the bribing, persuading and promise-making we did was exhausting, not to mention expensive.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“The Sordish Council of Radio and T..."
entries.dialogueText: “The Sordish Council of Radio and Television should prevent disrespectful language, especially towards our elected leaders.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Any good politician wouldn't let t..."
entries.dialogueText: “Any good politician wouldn't let that stop them from making a beneficial deal.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“It’s good to have a free and democ..."
entries.dialogueText: “It’s good to have a free and democratic debate in front of the eyes of the people. Even though television ownership still isn't the majority, plenty of radio listeners tuned in.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Any political opponent would have..."
entries.dialogueText: “Any political opponent would have done what we did. There was too much chaos after '51, and everything weakened Alphonso.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“I would still be wary of his and M..."
entries.dialogueText: “I would still be wary of his and Mr. Manger's intentions.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“I wouldn't be surprised if Alphons..."
entries.dialogueText: “I wouldn't be surprised if Alphonso would be willing to concede more due to this fact.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Diplomacy is the way, 99 percent o..."
entries.dialogueText: “Diplomacy is the way, 99 percent of the time.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Yeah, so many people in the party..."
entries.dialogueText: “Yeah, so many people in the party approached me and praised our course of action. They thought the USP was fractured enough and didn't need further tension.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“I think it would be wise to rememb..."
entries.dialogueText: “I think it would be wise to remember that after the civil war, all the global and regional powers wanted a piece of Sordland. Like sharks in the Antacean Sea.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“I wouldn't say it worked, Petr. So..."
entries.dialogueText: “I wouldn't say it worked, Petr. Sordland will truly start working under our leadership very soon.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Such is the nature of geopolitics...."
entries.dialogueText: “Such is the nature of geopolitics. Our national self-interest should be preserved with as little damage done to human dignity and rights as possible.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“I agree with you, Anton, and I'll..."
entries.dialogueText: “I agree with you, Anton, and I'll always support you, but you know my motto. If something works, don't break it.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“No matter how much people criticiz..."
entries.dialogueText: “No matter how much people criticize Soll these days, the Colonel is the reason why Sordland can stand mostly independent in this age."

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“They smelled weakness, and thanks..."
entries.dialogueText: “They smelled weakness, and thanks to initiatives of the Soll government, and the technocrats, the nation survived those hardships.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“The energy topic is gaining import..."
entries.dialogueText: “The energy topic is gaining importance again with the tensions in the Antacean Sea. I'm keeping a close watch on the situation.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“We don't want to find ourselves in..."
entries.dialogueText: “We don't want to find ourselves in the energy crisis situation of the early 1930s, where nations like Rumburg and Lespia leeched off our weakened position and charged us triple the cost per cubic ton.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Lucian pulled out a pen and took a..."
entries.dialogueText: Lucian pulled out a pen and took a few notes.

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“From our diplomatic channels, we c..."
entries.dialogueText: “From our diplomatic channels, we can tell that Lespia is still very interested in Sordish petrol, whereas Rumburg wants more gas resources.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I try to tread that difficult path..."
entries.dialogueText: “I try to tread that difficult path to the best of my ability.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Deivid coughed a bit and then conti..."
entries.dialogueText: Deivid coughed a bit and then continued talking.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The room went silent and no one ste..."
entries.dialogueText: The room went silent and no one stepped forward. It was noticeable how much people respected Wisci. He carried the soul of Sordland as a symbol of the past.

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Any further comments, esteemed cab..."
entries.dialogueText: “Any further comments, esteemed cabinet members?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The power structure behind the sce..."
entries.dialogueText: “The power structure behind the scenes shouldn't matter much to us.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Anytime Rumburg enters the 'play',..."
entries.dialogueText: “Anytime Rumburg enters the 'play', crap hits the fan.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I doubt he would allow it. It migh..."
entries.dialogueText: “I doubt he would allow it. It might hurt his hotel businesses around Port Grim.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Well, we can continue official dia..."
entries.dialogueText: “Well, we can continue official dialogue after this. It might lead to a more substantial agreement.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Alphonso's Minister of Foreign Aff..."
entries.dialogueText: “Alphonso's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Keres, coordinated the previous trade agreement, but is no longer working at the Ministry.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Of course, we are pushing to estab..."
entries.dialogueText: “Of course, we are pushing to establish a stronger relationship. But in the short term, this method is the one that could yield results.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Haha! One way to put it, Mr. Presi..."
entries.dialogueText: “Haha! One way to put it, Mr. President.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Petr kept grinning. The rest of the..."
entries.dialogueText: Petr kept grinning. The rest of the room wasn't feeling it.

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Dung business.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Dung business.”

entries.dialogueText: “Allowing more market economics to determine the value and output of our energy is aligned with our economic plan.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“A potential mistake when our trade..."
entries.dialogueText: “A potential mistake when our traders use our dependence on them against us.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I concur with Mr. Lancea. This is..."
entries.dialogueText: “I concur with Mr. Lancea. This is a distinct possibility.”

entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“We are at a much stronger position..."
entries.dialogueText: “We are at a much stronger position to negotiate either way. Lucian's information gives us an extra edge in talks.”

entries.dialogueText: “They never revealed much about their involvement to me, but I always had the feeling that Alphonso's crew was more linked to Gasom than they seemed.”
